# Panel

PanelContainer: the panel's own surface, at a fixed or the provider's width.

Also asked as: right panel, detail panel, side pane, slide-over, sheet, side sheet, off-canvas, right sidebar, side panel, inspector.

> Implemented as `PanelContainer` in the source and exported as `Panel`. Import the exported name; read the source under the implementation name.

**Import:** `import { Panel } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Panel/Panel.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Panel/Panel.stories.jsx` — FullComposition, MinimalHeaderAndBody, WidthFromProvider, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Panel/Panel.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.slow` · exit `spatial.default`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations · Motion.

## Usage

Use `Panel` for context or a focused task beside the page's main content — a
detail view opened from a list, a filter set, a secondary thread — where
leaving the page behind, as a `Modal` does, would lose that context. For
something that must be decided before the page continues, use `Modal`
instead.

Fixed action components cover the common icons: `PanelBackAction`,
`PanelCloseAction`, `PanelMoreAction`, `PanelUpAction`, `PanelDownAction`,
`PanelNewTabAction` and `PanelViewSwitcher`, each a labeled `IconButton` with
its glyph and accessible name already set.

## Motion

Panel reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-slow` | Docked: slides in while the page resizes. Floating: spatial.default over the page. Narrow: slides over with a Backdrop. |
| exit | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Floating panels leave on spatial.fast. |

## Best practices

### Give the panel room to read. {#give-the-panel-room-to-read}

Below its default width the title wraps and the body stops being scannable.

Do: Default width.
Don't: Squeezed to a narrow strip.

### Keep the header to one cue. {#keep-the-header-to-one-cue}

An icon, a subheader and a footer together bury the title; pick the one the task needs.

Do: Title with an icon.
Don't: Icon, back action and subheader all on, burying the title.

### Title the panel with the object. {#title-the-panel-with-the-object}

The title names what the panel shows, so someone who opened it from elsewhere still knows.

Do: The object it shows: “Session notes”.
Don't: A generic “Details” that does not name the object.

### Share one width across a page's panels with `PanelProvider`. {#share-one-width-across-a-page-s-panels-with-panelprovider}

Wrap the region that can open panels in a `PanelProvider`, and read or change
the shared width with `usePanelManager`, so multiple panels opened over time
stay the same size instead of each picking its own.

```jsx
<PanelProvider>
    <PanelContainer>
        <PanelHeader title="Student detail" actions={<PanelCloseAction onClick={close} />} />
        <PanelBody>...</PanelBody>
    </PanelContainer>
</PanelProvider>
```

### Reach for the fixed action components before building your own. {#reach-for-the-fixed-action-components-before-building-your-own}

`PanelBackAction`, `PanelCloseAction` and the rest already carry the right
icon, label and compact spacing — building a custom `IconButton` for the same
job only risks a different icon or label than the rest of the system uses.

## Accessibility

- **A labeled region.** `PanelHeader`'s title is a `Heading`, giving the
  panel a heading assistive technology can navigate to directly.
- **Fixed actions are already named.** Each action component sets its own
  accessible name (for example, `PanelCloseAction` is always labeled
  "Close"), so there is nothing extra to pass.
- **`usePanelManager` outside a provider fails loudly.** Calling it without a
  `PanelProvider` ancestor throws, rather than silently falling back, so a
  missing provider is caught during development.

## Parts

1. **Container** (`PanelContainer`). The outer surface. Its `width` falls back to the nearest `PanelProvider`'s width, then to `--panel-width-default` (400); inside the Frame's Panel area it fills the area instead.
2. **Header** (`PanelHeader`). An optional back action, an optional title icon, the title, and an action group (close, more, …).
3. **Subheader** (`PanelSubheader`). An optional row of secondary content under the header: tabs, a filter summary.
4. **Body** (`PanelBody`). The main content, which scrolls.
5. **Footer** (`PanelFooter`). Actions that commit a change, with an optional `PanelDisclaimer` for small print beside them.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | An overlay surface with a leading edge. |
| Hovered | Nothing changes on the panel. |
| Pressed | Nothing changes on the panel. |
| Focused | Not focusable. Focus goes to the fixed actions and the content. |
| Disabled | A panel has no disabled state. Disable the controls in it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Ground and edge | `--ds-surface-overlay`; `--ds-border` at `--border-default` on the leading edge. |
| Header | Padding `--space-100` and `--space-150`; `--space-075` between its parts; `--border-default` rule below. |
| Action group | `--space-025` between actions. |
| Subheader | Padding `--space-075` and `--space-150`; `--border-default` rule below. |
| Body | Padding `--space-150`. |
| Footer | Padding `--space-100` and `--space-150`, `--space-100` between its parts; rule above; disclaimer in `--body-small`, `--ds-text-subtle`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the panel for its subject: "Session details". | Title it "Panel" or "Details". |
| Keep the disclaimer to one line. | Put instructions in the footer that belong in the body. |
| Name the footer action for its result: "Done", "Save". | Use "OK" or "Submit". |
